Capture the Computational Environment of a Session

Source: R/repro_environment.R
capture_environment.Rd

Records the software environment of the running R session into a structured, serializable snapshot: the R version, the platform and operating system, the locale, and the attached and loaded packages with their versions. A submission is only reproducible if a reviewer can recreate the environment that produced it, so capturing that environment alongside the data and outputs is a core reproducibility concern. This complements repro_manifest(), which hashes the data and output files, by recording the software that produced them.

Usage

capture_environment(info = NULL, file = NULL)

Arguments

info

A utils::sessionInfo()-like object to capture from. When NULL (the default), the running session is captured with utils::sessionInfo(). Supplying info makes capture testable with a synthetic session.

file

Optional path to write the snapshot to as JSON. When supplied, the snapshot is written there and the path is returned invisibly; otherwise the repro_environment object is returned.

Value

An object of class repro_environment: a list with r_version, platform, os, locale, a packages tibble (columns package, version, attached), the counts n_packages and n_attached, and captured (the capture time). When file is supplied, the path to the written JSON snapshot is returned invisibly instead. The JSON document carries an env_type, a schema_version, the capture time, the source package and version, the R version, platform, OS, locale, the package count, and a packages array. It has a print method.

Details

The snapshot is read entirely from utils::sessionInfo(): the attached non-base packages (otherPkgs) and the loaded-but-not-attached packages (loadedOnly), each with the version sessionInfo() reports. Base packages are omitted because sessionInfo() records no version for them and they track the R version. Capture is robust when optional fields are absent.

This is a descriptive/integrity helper, not an indicator. It emits no R4SUB evidence, carries no severity, and does not change the pass/fail or score of any indicator. Compare two snapshots with compare_environments().

See also

compare_environments() to diff two snapshots, and repro_manifest() for the companion file-hash manifest.

Examples

# Capture the current session
env <- capture_environment()
env$r_version
#> [1] "R version 4.6.2 (2026-10-29)"
env$packages
#> # A tibble: 50 × 3
#>    package  version attached
#>    <chr>    <chr>   <lgl>   
#>  1 R6       2.6.1   FALSE   
#>  2 askpass  1.2.1   FALSE   
#>  3 bslib    0.12.0  FALSE   
#>  4 cachem   1.1.0   FALSE   
#>  5 callr    3.8.0   FALSE   
#>  6 cli      3.6.6   FALSE   
#>  7 compiler 4.6.2   FALSE   
#>  8 curl     8.1.0   FALSE   
#>  9 desc     1.4.3   FALSE   
#> 10 digest   0.6.39  FALSE   
#> # ℹ 40 more rows

# Write a portable JSON snapshot
f <- capture_environment(file = file.path(tempdir(), "env.json"))
#> ✔ Wrote environment snapshot (51 packages) to /tmp/RtmpXgcl4F/env.json
file.exists(f)
#> [1] TRUE
